issue_context.title: JSRuntime: browser js loader rejects with an error Event, not an Error
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

If loading js were to fail in a browser context with the global output format, the promise would be rejected with an error _Event_, not an Error object. This is not intuitive, and is inconsistent with real `import()`s in browsers and across how we implement this in other environments.

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Should reject with an Error object instead. Real `import()`s can reject with a TypeError such as `TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:5000/foo.js`.

## 😯 Current Behavior

If fetching the module fails, the promise returned by `import()` rejects with a DOM Error event.

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/dea272f0708fdabfe11f844f189df6421e7a3b65/packages/runtimes/js/src/loaders/browser/js-loader.js#L20

## 💁 Possible Solution

Create our own error in the browser js loader that is shaped like what real `import()`s in browsers reject with in this case.
comments:
> Create our own error in the browser js loader

That would be here:

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/dea272f0708fdabfe11f844f189df6421e7a3b65/packages/runtimes/js/src/loaders/browser/js-loader.js#L17-L20
Hi, I'd love to contribute! Can I work on this issue?

review_comments: This should probably just be `new Error`. I don't think TypeError makes sense here

Chrome and Firefox do use `TypeError`:
```
> import("http://google.com")
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://google.com/
```

I don't think `TypeError` is specced somewhere though because the behaviour is implementation defined

https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-call-runtime-semantics-evaluation
https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostimportmoduledynamically

https://github.com/GoogleChromeLabs/dynamic-import-polyfill/blob/5ae321654a96c5e99b23b7cdabe10bc6159caaaa/initialize.mjs#L59
Do you think we can keep `TypeError` to be inline with browsers behaviour though?
Should we somehow attach the original error so people can determine why it failed?
